language.script_notes: Latin alphabet with distinctive Polish diacritics — ł, ż, ż, ę, ą, ś, ć — not found in Czech/Slovak. Street suffixes: Ulica, Plac, Aleja, Rondo, Droga.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White posts with a red vertical stripe on one side only — a distinctive, near-unique Poland tell.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Slim rounded post with the single-side red stripe.
road_furniture.line_paint: White outside/white inside lines; double solid center lines common on many roads.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; birch trees frequently line rural roads on both sides.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Poland's triangular warning signs are the only ones in the world with a thin red outline and yellow fill. Concrete 'holey' utility poles are common, but Poland's holes stop about half a metre above the ground rather than running all the way down as in Hungary/Romania; poles are sometimes doubled or joined in an A-frame.

architecture.roof_style: Simple pitched roofs on detached single-family homes nationwide; red/orange, black or brown roofing common.
architecture.roof_material: Clay/concrete tile common in towns; corrugated sheet metal roofing common on rural houses, similar to the Baltic states.
architecture.wall_construction: Plain stone/masonry walls finished in light or pastel-coloured stucco is the default residential look; Soviet-era panel apartment blocks (blokowisko) common in cities; Gothic brick churches and town halls in historic centers (Kraków, Gdańsk, Toruń).
architecture.wall_color_palette: Pastel stucco (cream, pale yellow, pale blue) on houses; red brick Gothic in historic town centers; grey concrete panel blocks in Soviet-era housing estates.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Gothic red-brick churches and town halls (Kraków, Toruń, Gdańsk's Hanseatic-influenced old town); Soviet-era panel apartment blocks; detached pastel-stucco single-family houses in rural/suburban areas; wooden village houses further east.

nature.vegetation: Vast flat wheat, rye and potato fields dominate central Poland ('the breadbasket'), often stretching to the horizon; birch trees commonly line rural roads; dense forest in the north and southeast.
nature.terrain: Overwhelmingly flat to gently rolling across the North European Plain; the Sudetes and Carpathian (Tatra) mountains rise only along the southern border.
nature.climate_signature: Temperate continental; grassy fields on both sides of rural roads with a row of trees is a very common recurring shot.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate, black text, blue EU strip on the left with 'PL'.
vehicles.plate_format: X1 2345 or X1 234J-style groupings (province letter code, then a mix of letters/digits).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Standard mixed European fleet; older Polish Street View coverage is notable for a Google car with a visible black roof rack — a well-known dating/meta clue.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of Gen 3 and Gen 4; older coverage (identifiable partly by the visible black roof rack on the car) still common in rural areas.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage in cities and along main roads; some rural gaps and older imagery further from major routes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Central European architecture, Slavic language family, similar road furniture styles
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Polish diacritics (ł, ż, ą, ę) differ from Czech's ř/ě/ů; Poland's single-side-red-stripe bollard and uniquely red-outlined yellow warning triangles are absent in Czechia; Polish holey poles stop partway down rather than running to the ground.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Concrete 'holey' utility poles appear in all three countries
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Poland's pole holes stop about half a metre above ground level; Hungary's and Romania's holes run all the way down to the base — a reliable distinguishing detail once you know to look for it.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar corrugated-metal-roofed rural houses, flat agricultural terrain, similar climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Polish language and diacritics differ sharply from Lithuanian/Latvian/Estonian; Poland's red-striped bollard and red-outlined warning triangle are absent in the Baltic states.
